question_text: A tea estate on a hillside uses a hoist to bring crates of picked leaves up to its factory. A trolley is pulled along a straight track from the loading shed $P$ at the bottom of the slope to the factory $Q$ at the top. Diagram 1 shows a side view. $R$ is the point vertically below $Q$ on the same horizontal level as $P$. The track $PQ$ is $240$ m long and $Q$ is $76$ m higher than $P$.

parts.text: Calculate the angle of elevation, $\theta$, of $Q$ from $P$.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Calculate the horizontal distance $PR$.
parts.label: b

parts.text:
The track is made of two identical straight steel rails, each as long as $PQ$. Diagram 2 shows the uniform cross-section of one rail. The rails rest on trestles which can hold a total load of at most $9.5$ tonnes. ($1$ tonne $= 1000$ kg.)

Some information about the hoist is given below.
Density of steel: $7850$ kg/m$^3$
Mass of the empty trolley: $460$ kg
Mass of one full crate of leaves: $32$ kg
The hoist runs from 0630 to 1430 each day.
The trolley is the only one on the track. It takes $40$ minutes to be loaded, go up, be unloaded and come back down, and it starts the next trip at once.
The factory earns $\$28$ from each full crate of leaves.

The estate manager says that the leaves brought up by the hoist earn the factory at least $\$8000$ a day. Only full crates are carried. Justify, with calculations, whether the manager is correct.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: Area of cross-section $= 2200$ mm$^2 = 0.0022$ m$^2$. Mass of two rails $= 2 \times 0.0022 \times 240 \times 7850 = 8289.6$ kg. Greatest mass of crates $= 9500 - 8289.6 - 460 = 750.4$ kg, so at most $23$ crates a trip. Trips a day $= 12$. Greatest earnings $= 23 \times 12 \times \$28 = \$7728 < \$8000$, so the manager is not correct.

parts.text: It is given that $y = 3\sin^2 x - 7\cos^2 x$. Show that $y$ can be written as $p\cos 2x + q$, where $p$ and $q$ are integers to be found. Hence explain why $y$ can never be equal to $-8$.
parts.label: c
parts.answer: $p = -5$, $q = -2$, so $y = -5\cos 2x - 2$. Since $-1 \le \cos 2x \le 1$, $-7 \le y \le 3$; the least value of $y$ is $-7 > -8$, so $y$ can never equal $-8$.

question_text: A survey recorded the time, in minutes, that each of 200 workers living in Town P took to travel to work one morning. The cumulative frequency curve shows the distribution of these journey times.

parts.text: Use the curve to estimate
parts.label: a

subparts.text: the median journey time,
subparts.label: i

subparts.text: the interquartile range of the journey times.
subparts.label: ii

parts.text: A journey that lasts at least $55$ minutes is classed as a long commute. Estimate the number of workers in Town P who had a long commute.
parts.label: b

parts.text: Two of the 200 workers are picked at random to be interviewed. Find the probability that exactly one of them had a long commute.
parts.label: c

parts.text: The same survey was carried out on 200 workers living in Town Q, and the box-and-whisker plot shows the distribution of their journey times. Suppose a cumulative frequency curve is drawn for Town Q on the same axes as the curve for Town P. Describe how the curve for Town Q would look different from the curve for Town P, and give a reason for your answer.
parts.label: d
parts.answer: The curve for Town Q is steeper around the median than the curve for Town P: its lower part lies to the right of Town P's curve and its upper part lies to the left, and the two curves cross at the median, $38$ minutes. Reason: the medians are the same but the interquartile range for Town Q ($10$ minutes) is smaller than that for Town P ($16$ minutes), so the middle half of Town Q's journey times is less spread out.

Diagram 1 — a cumulative frequency curve on a graph-paper grid, titled 'Town P'. Horizontal axis labelled 'Time (minutes)', running from 10 to 70, with numbered major gridlines at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70 and ten small squares between consecutive majors (one small square = 1 minute). Vertical axis labelled 'Cumulative frequency', running from 0 to 200, with numbered major gridlines at 0, 20, 40, ..., 200 and ten small squares between consecutive majors (one small square = 2 workers). Diagram 2 — a horizontal box-and-whisker plot, titled 'Town Q', drawn above a number line labelled 'Time (minutes)' that runs from 10 to 70 with numbered ticks at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70 and a small tick at every 1 minute (or on a grid with one small square = 1 minute). Left whisker end (minimum) at 12, left edge of box (lower quartile) at 33, median line inside the box at 38, right edge of box (upper quartile) at 43, right whisker end (maximum) at 68. The five values are NOT written on the plot; they are to be read from the scale.

verdict.key_verdict: The setter's key and the blind examiner agree on every part, and my own working confirms each value, so the key stands.

blind_answers.(d): Town Q's curve is steeper through the middle (between about CF 50 and CF 150, i.e. t = 33 to 43) because its interquartile range is 10 minutes (43 - 33) compared with 16 for Town P, so the middle half of journey times is more tightly clustered. question_text: Figure 1 shows a solid block of candle wax in the shape of a prism. question_text:
Two blank sets of axes are drawn below, labelled Diagram 1 and Diagram 2. On each of them the point $P(-1, 1)$ has been plotted to show the scale.
Draw a sketch of each curve on the diagram stated, making clear the shape of the curve and how it behaves near the axes.

parts.text: On Diagram 1, the curve $y = -\frac{3}{x^{2}}$.
parts.label: a
parts.answer: Two branches, both below the $x$-axis, one on each side of the $y$-axis and symmetric about the $y$-axis, passing through $(-1, -3)$ and $(1, -3)$; $y < 0$ throughout, each branch going down steeply beside the $y$-axis (vertical asymptote) and flattening towards the $x$-axis (horizontal asymptote) without touching either axis.

parts.text: On Diagram 2, the curve $y = 5^{-x}$.
parts.label: b
parts.answer: Smooth decreasing (exponential decay) curve lying wholly above the $x$-axis, crossing the $y$-axis at $(0, 1)$ and passing through $(-1, 5)$; rises steeply to the left and flattens towards the $x$-axis (horizontal asymptote) on the right without touching it.

The axes cross at the centre of the diagram, so all four quadrants are shown with equal space; there is room for about 3 units left and right of O and about 6 units above and below O (same unit length on both axes). In each diagram one solid dot is plotted in the second quadrant, 1 unit to the left of the y-axis and 1 unit above the x-axis, labelled P(-1, 1). Nothing else is drawn: no curves, no tick marks, no other points.

parts.text: Find, in simplest surd form, the values of $x$ which satisfy $\sqrt{5x^{2} - 3} + 2 = 3x$.
parts.label: a

parts.text: The diagram shows a circle through the points $L$, $M$ and $N$. The straight line $KM$ touches the circle at $M$. The point $K$ is placed so that angle $MKL$ is equal to angle $MLN$.
parts.label: b

subparts.text: Show that triangles $KML$ and $LNM$ are similar.
subparts.label: i
subparts.answer: $\angle KML = \angle LNM$ (alternate segment theorem) and $\angle MKL = \angle NLM$ (given), so triangle $KML$ is similar to triangle $LNM$ (AA).

subparts.text: Name the special quadrilateral $KMNL$, explaining clearly how you know.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.answer: Trapezium: $\angle KLM = \angle LMN$ (third angles of similar triangles), these are alternate angles, so $KL$ is parallel to $MN$ — one pair of parallel sides.

Draw the segments KM (part of the tangent, extended a little beyond M on the other side to show it is a tangent) and KL. Labels: K, L, M, N at their points. No lengths, no angle values and no centre are marked; no parallel arrows and no equal-angle marks are drawn.
